I've attached a current subprocessor inventory CSV (latest snapshot as of today) and a CAIQ crosswalk workbook. Quick summary up front:

Hi Elena, Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Marcus. I pulled together the attestation materials you'll need for procurement. Summary answers (short):
- PHI exposure: Redwood does not process PHI by default. For customers who ingest PHI, we offer Private deployment options and contractual safeguards. None of our listed subprocessors are permitted to use customer plaintext data for training or model development.
- Key management: KeyVaultCorp provides envelope encryption for runtime keys; Redwood holds zero-knowledge of customer-managed keys when KMS is customer-provisioned.
- Logging: LogStream Inc. collects aggregated telemetry (metrics, anonymized traces). No application payloads are forwarded to external analytics partners.

Attached are: a SOC 2 Type II summary (redwood_soc2_type2_summary_20260915.pdf), the CAIQ crosswalk workbook (already attached by Marcus), and a short KMS controls extract for KeyVaultCorp (kms_provider_controls_kvcorp.pdf). I've also uploaded the full evidence bundle to a shared Drive folder and provided the link below.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_drive_link (contains SOC report redactions, CAIQ crosswalk, subprocessor CSV, and selected control evidence logs)

Two notes for procurement:
1) If Greenleaf requires original SOC 2 Type II reports (unredacted), we can coordinate a controlled attestation exchange under an NDA with our legal team — please flag this.
2) If you need a short cover letter on subprocessors and residency for your packet, I can prepare a one-page attestation by EOD 9/16.

Marcus/Hannah — I recommend we provide the one-page attestation proactively; it reduces back-and-forth.

Regards,
